clue.text: Job with appeal after time

indicators.note: after places the appeal piece behind the time piece in the finished word

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
to appeal for something is to request it

explanation.surface: A job application that comes with an appeal lodged after the deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work someone has to do, an assignment or chore.

clue.text: Material error, not good, in silly tat

indicators.note: in sets the shortened error inside the rearranged rubbish
silly suggests the following word is muddled and rearranged

parts.note: tat is cheap, tasteless goods; its letters are rearranged

indicators.note: not good tells you to drop the letter standing for good, G

parts.note: a gaffe is a blunder

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that a fabric mistake has been made in a pile of silly trinkets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like an adjective for the error but is the definition; tat is British slang for cheap, tacky goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous woven fabric, often silk, used for dresses, so it is a kind of cloth.

clue.text: See placid broadcast on uniform postal service

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattering widely, so the preceding letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: nine letters to be rearranged
livery is the distinctive uniform worn by servants or staff

explanation.surface: A calm programme being aired about uniforms.
explanation.definitionFit: Special delivery is a Royal Mail service that guarantees next-day arrival of a letter or parcel.

clue.text: Irreverent type using ample herbs differently

indicators.note: differently says the letters are to be arranged in another way

parts.note: ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cook who flouts convention by using lots of herbs in an unusual way.
explanation.definitionFit: A blasphemer speaks disrespectfully about sacred things, the epitome of an irreverent person.

clue.text: Catch up with a climber

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to nail a criminal is to catch them
taken as written

explanation.surface: Catching up with a mountaineer on the slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody vine of tropical forests that climbs up tree trunks toward the light.

clue.text: Small steps on projecting part in interstellar craft

indicators.note: in a down entry, on puts the earlier pieces above the next one

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
paces are steps
the hip is a projecting part of the body or of a roof

explanation.surface: Tiny steps along a protruding ledge inside a starship.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceship is a vehicle built to travel through outer space, so it is a craft for journeys between stars.

clue.text: Drone on soft mound

indicators.note: in a down entry, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a drone is a low continuous hum
P, piano, is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A buzzing bee or aircraft over a soft hillock.
explanation.definitionFit: A hump is a rounded raised bump in the ground, like a small hillock or bulge.

clue.text: Profit easily made from food only emperor ordered

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are arranged into a fresh sequence

parts.note: fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An emperor who placed an order for nothing but food.
explanation.walkthrough: Money for old rope is a British idiom for payment that requires almost no effort.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes money earned for very little work, an easy gain obtained without trouble.

clue.text: Think ahead after ruin, losing weight

indicators.note: losing weight says the letter standing for weight, W, is dropped
after places the forward piece behind the ruin piece

parts.note: to wreck something is to ruin it
on means forward or ahead, as in 'go on'

explanation.surface: A dieter planning ahead after their plans went to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to suppose or believe, an informal synonym for holding an opinion.

clue.text: Flower is back in clear area

indicators.note: in places that turned word inside the clear-plus-area pair

parts.note: clear of obstacles means free

indicators.note: back means the small word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A flower has returned to an open space.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a fragrant South African plant grown for its bell-shaped blooms, a popular cut flower.

clue.text: Avoids work, keeping six servants

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to skive is British slang for dodging work
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Shirkers employing half a dozen domestic staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Both skive (to dodge work) and skivvy (a menial servant) are British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A skivvy is British slang for a lowly domestic servant who does menial chores.

clue.text: Guy enthralled by interior of royal residence in handbook

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive within, so the guy sits inside
interior of keeps only the inside letters of the named building

parts.note: a palace is a royal residence; its inner letters are kept
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A man captivated by the inside of a palace, as described in a guidebook.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is an annual reference book of calendars and facts, a kind of handbook.

clue.text: Jubilant about one manager, initially popular, being removed

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the joyful word wraps the rest

parts.note: elated means jubilant
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: initially keeps just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of manager
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Fans celebrating a popular football manager being sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Being eliminated means being knocked out or got rid of, as a team removed from a competition.

clue.text: Mistake in party politics

indicators.note: in says the answer is sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: An error made within the world of party politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a typing or printing slip, a small error in written text.

clue.text: Measure designed to protect new online identification

indicators.note: to protect means enclosing something safely within
designed means freshly planned, so the letters are put into a new pattern

parts.note: letters to rearrange
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A security step brought in to safeguard novel internet ID.
explanation.definitionFit: A username is the name a person uses to log in to a website or computer account.

clue.text: Have help, lost or otherwise in disarray

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters take another order

parts.note: fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone who has had help, or else got lost, and is now in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: All over the shop is British slang for scattered or in a chaotic state.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means scattered everywhere and badly organised, a state of complete confusion.

clue.text: Revive, swimming near island with friend

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters are moving about freely into a new order

parts.note: letters to rearrange
I is the abbreviation for island
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A swimmer brought round near an island by a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: To reanimate is to bring back to life or restore vigour, so it means to revive.

clue.text: Officer with bag, carrying work around, useful in many ways

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the bag holds the work

parts.note: a purse is a small bag

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the short word for work is read backwards

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: An army officer with a handbag full of paperwork, ready for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: General-purpose describes something designed for a wide range of uses rather than one specific job.

clue.text: Serious gain established

parts.note: to earn is to gain
EST is the abbreviation for established, seen on shop signs

explanation.surface: Serious financial gains that have become settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and serious in intention, not joking or frivolous.

clue.text: Be quiet with status diminished

parts.note: sh is the instruction to be quiet
rank is position or status

explanation.surface: Advice to keep silent now that one has lost standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrank, the past tense of shrink, means became smaller, just as diminished does.

clue.text: Sound of healthy acclaim

indicators.note: sound of says we want a word pronounced like the following one

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: The noise of hearty applause.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail someone is to acclaim or praise them enthusiastically, as in hailing a hero.

clue.text: Start of hype heralding stirring film with Sean Connery

indicators.note: stirring means mixing up, so the letters are churned into a new order
start of keeps just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of hype
letters to be stirred together with the first piece

explanation.surface: Publicity announcing a thrilling Connery movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' reads as describing the film but is the anagram signal; Highlander (1986) has Connery as the swordsman Ramirez.
explanation.definitionFit: Highlander is the 1986 fantasy film in which Sean Connery plays the immortal mentor Ramirez.

clue.text: Scavenger with cry of triumph securing desire

indicators.note: securing means holding fast within, so the cry encloses the desire

parts.note: ha is a triumphant exclamation
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A scavenging animal crowing in triumph after getting what it wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is an African carnivore known for feeding on carrion left by other predators.

clue.text: Book club giving away last pen

indicators.note: giving away last means the final letter of the club is dropped

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A book club handing out its final pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests the book club, but it is a golf club; Biro is the British everyday word for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A Biro is a ballpoint pen, the brand name having become the common British word for one.

clue.text: Article with endless value about Simon and Garfunkel song

indicators.note: endless means the word for value loses its final letter

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
merit is worth or value
ca, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on the lasting worth of a Simon and Garfunkel number.
explanation.definitionFit: America is a 1968 Simon and Garfunkel song from the album Bookends about a road trip.

clue.text: Certainly nothing right in middle of speech, ugly thing

indicators.note: in puts the earlier pieces inside the kept central letters
middle of keeps the central letters of the word that follows

parts.note: the two middle letters of speech
yes means certainly
O looks like zero, nothing
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Insisting there is nothing correct at the heart of a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something unpleasant to look at, such as an ugly building.

clue.text: Tool's essential difficulty noticed

parts.note: key means crucial or essential
being in a hole is being in difficulty
saw means noticed

explanation.surface: Someone spotted the fundamental problem with a piece of equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyhole saw is a narrow-bladed saw for cutting small holes or curves, a woodworking implement.

clue.text: Run into swarm going west

indicators.note: going west in an across entry means reading from right to left

parts.note: to teem is to swarm

explanation.surface: Bumping into a crowd heading westward.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet someone can mean to encounter them by chance, just as running into someone does.
